commit_message:
access/tiering: fix adversarial-review findings; real GDSF aging (review of #18, #20) (#28)

* xdol.access: fix adversarial-review findings; AccessLog is a Mapping

- Warn once when a key does not survive a JSON round trip; document str keys.
- track_access never raises from tracking: size falls back to 0 without len.
- An event without "n" keeps the size; replay is order-independent (max recency,
  min first_seen, size from the latest access), consistent with merge_stats.
- A torn last line gets a newline before the first append; the file is read in
  binary and each line decoded inside the try (undecodable lines are skipped).
- Unknown ops, and release/unpin on an unknown key, create no phantom entries.
- AccessStats is frozen (no shared mutable state handed out).
- AccessLog is a Mapping of key -> AccessStats (stats() kept as alias of get);
  merge_stats takes Mappings, no duck typing.
- track_access: clock/tag alongside a tracker is an error (no silent divergence).
- compact() documents that it is safe only with no other writer.
- Tests killing the reviewer's surviving mutants.

* xdol.tiering: fix adversarial-review findings; real GDSF aging

- budget_bytes=0: a write drops any hot copy instead of leaving it stale.
- prefetch records a read served from cold and its release step never releases
  the keys it was asked for (sweep(..., exclude=)); local_paths raises
  FileNotFoundError if the file is still missing.
- GDSF per Cherkasova: H = L + F*C/S fixed at access time, L := H of the
  released key, F counts accesses since admission. Kept inside the policy via a
  new PlacementPolicy.on_hot_access hook; keys already hot are seeded with their
  logged frequency.
- Running hot-bytes total instead of an O(n) sum per op.
- TieredStore has no clock argument: it uses the tracker's clock.
- Startup over an existing hot store records nothing and reads no values: sizes
  come from the log, else the file size, else are learnt on the next hot hit.
- admit_after_reads <= 1 always admits.
- __setitem__ raises TypeError for a value without len before any write.
- __delitem__ drops the hot copy before deleting from cold.
- One exceeds_watermark helper; dead code removed; single-threaded documented.
- Tests: aging, bounded local_paths, overwrite/delete bookkeeping, startup with
  an existing hot store, admit_after_reads=1, item larger than budget, hot write
  error state, no stray warning.

* tests(tiering): hot Files use permanent deletion (Windows trash needs pywin32 and warns)

* tiering/access: re-review cuts — on_hot_drop (no policy-entry leak), release never reads the value, AccessLog keeps identity, private _exceeds_watermark, one hot-bytes name
